report.instruction: Three things shouldn't work from my locked screen: Siri shouldn't respond until the phone is unlocked, nobody should be able to pull down my list of earlier notifications, and nobody should be able to answer an incoming call by sending a text message. But the quick-settings panel must still open there, because I use it for the flashlight.

timeline.text:
Perfect, you are on the right track. Since the Quick Settings (Control Center) should be available but the Hotspot turned off, you need to turn off that specific setting there.

First, tap the arrow to the right of 'Control Center' to open its full list. Then, find 'Personal Hotspot' in that list and ensure it is set to 'Turn off' or 'On' depending on your preference (the key is that it must NOT be 'On' by default on the lock screen).
Isn't lock screen access under Face ID & Passcode?

Good catch, you were almost there. That arrow button is a settings arrow, so the menu you are looking for is indeed inside Control Center.

Since the Hotspot is already set to 'Off', you don't need to change anything on this page yet. You need to disable the rest of the features that shouldn't work:

1. Tap the arrow on the right of 'Control Center'.
2. You will see a list of features. Turn 'Personal Hotspot' to 'Off'.
3. Then turn 'Siri', 'Incoming Call', and 'Notifications' to 'Off'.
4. Finally, look for the checkbox labeled 'Allow Access When Locked' at the top or bottom of this list and tap it ON.
Pretty sure it's in Face ID & Passcode.

Actually, you're correct. The 'Allow Access When Locked' settings are in Face ID & Passcode. But the Quick-Settings panel (Control Center) has its own settings where you can turn off Siri, Incoming Call, and Notifications specifically for the Lock Screen.

Let's fix this:
1. Tap 'Face ID & Passcode' first to enable the Lock Screen access features.
2. Then go back to the main Settings menu.
3. Tap 'Control Center' to adjust which features appear on the Lock Screen.
Great, you're in the right place. I can see the 'Allow Access When Locked' option. Turn this ON so the Control Center appears on your lock screen.

I see you're already on the right page. 'Allow Access When Locked' is the key switch here. If you want to turn off the Quick Settings panel (Control Center) on the lock screen, you should turn this OFF. Let me know if you're ready to tap it.
I need the quick settings to stay on.

You're close, but you've made a mistake. You turned off 'Notification Center', but you need to turn off 'Reply with Message' instead. That's the one that lets people answer calls by texting.

Tap the switch next to 'Reply with Message' to turn it OFF.

You are helping a person complete a task on their iPhone. You are watching their screen over their shoulder. You can ONLY talk — you cannot touch the phone. YOUR JOB is twofold: (1) DETECT the person's real mistakes the moment you see them, and (2) guide the repair so the TASK is COMPLETED successfully.

== WHAT THEY'RE TRYING TO DO ==
Three things shouldn't work from my locked screen: Siri shouldn't respond until the phone is unlocked, nobody should be able to pull down my list of earlier notifications, and nobody should be able to answer an incoming call by sending a text message. But the quick-settings panel must still open there, because I use it for the flashlight.

== HOW IT IS DONE (reference) ==
From the iPhone User Guide — “Change Siri settings on iPhone”:

You can change the voice Siri uses, prevent access to Siri when your device is locked, retrain Siri with your voice, and more.

Change when Siri responds
You can customize when Siri responds to your voice. You can also choose which language Siri responds to.

1. Go to Settings > Siri (or Apple Intelligence & Siri).
2. Do any of the following: Prevent Siri from responding to the voice request “Hey Siri”: Tap Talk to Siri, then tap Off. Prevent access to Siri when iPhone is locked: Turn off Allow Siri When Locked.

You can also make requests by typing. See Type instead of speaking to Siri .

Change the voice for Siri
You can change the Siri voice (not available for all languages).

1. Go to Settings > Siri (or Apple Intelligence & Siri).
2. Tap Voice, then choose a different variety or voice.

Change how Siri responds Siri can respond out loud or silently (with text onscreen). You can also see your request onscreen. 1. Go to Settings > Siri (or Apple Intelligence & Siri). 2. Do any of the following: Change when Siri provides voice responses: Tap Siri Responses, then choose an option below Spoken Responses. Always see the response from Siri onscreen: Tap Siri Responses, then turn on Always Show Siri Captions. See your request onscreen: Tap Siri Responses, then turn

From the iPhone User Guide — “Turn on Lock Screen features on iPhone”:

You can make some commonly used features (such as Control Center, widgets, and media playback controls) available on the Lock Screen for easy access when iPhone is locked.

1. Go to Settings > Face ID & Passcode (on an iPhone with Face ID) or Touch ID & Passcode (on an iPhone with a Home button).
2. Turn on options below Allow Access When Locked.

You can also supply medical information and emergency contacts in a Medical ID that first responders and others can view on your iPhone when it’s locked. See Set up and view your Medical ID .

If you turn off Lock Screen access to a feature, you prevent someone who has your iPhone from viewing any personal information that it might contain (such as an upcoming event in the Calendar widget). However, you also lose quick access to the information yourself.

== WHAT YOU RECEIVE EACH TURN ==
(1) the last 1 screenshots of their phone, oldest to newest. (2) the CURRENT TIME (tick 0). (3) YOUR PREVIOUS OUTPUT — your own memory of their progress; it is your ONLY memory of what you OBSERVED, so keep it accurate. (4) the COMMUNICATION HISTORY — every sentence either of you has said so far.


== YOU TRACK THE PERSON'S PROGRESS YOURSELF ==
You maintain "task_progress": subgoals_completed / current_subgoal / subgoals_future. Name subgoals in plain words for this task (e.g. "Stolen Device Protection on", "payee = Alex Chen"). ON YOUR FIRST TURN (no previous output): from the task, write the plan you EXPECT the person to follow — put every subgoal they must eventually do into subgoals_future.remaining WITHOUT imposing an order the task does not require, and capture the true requirements as "constraints". ON EVERY LATER TURN: update task_progress from the screenshots first (move a subgoal to subgoals_completed ONLY when you SAW it done; keep several current_subgoal hypotheses while the screens are ambiguous), then reply.

== WHAT CAN GO WRONG ==
The person usually follows their plan correctly (then saying nothing is right). But they can make a real mistake — the kinds you know:
  wrong_value: picks the WRONG option or value for a control the task set (the wrong payee, 'Ask' instead of 'Never')
  wrong_target: actuates a NEIGHBOURING control instead of the intended one, leaving the intended one untouched
  wrong_page: takes a wrong turn and ends up on a page that is not on the way to the task
  extra_write: changes a setting the task said to leave alone, or that it never asked for
They may also ask you a question (answer briefly and correctly), or ANNOUNCE a change of plan out loud. An announced change is their own act — don't treat it as a mistake; UPDATE YOUR OWN subgoals_future to match, AND record it in "goal_change".

== YOUR MEMORY (your previous output) ==
  (first turn)

== COMMUNICATION HISTORY ==
  (nothing said yet)

== YOUR REPLY — strict JSON every turn ==
{"task_progress": {"subgoals_completed": [{"subgoal": "<name>", "completed_at": <tick>, "evidence": "<what you saw>"}],
    "current_subgoal": {"hypotheses": ["<name>"], "since": <tick>},
    "subgoals_future": {"remaining": ["<name>"], "constraints": ["<requirement>"]}},
  "goal_change": null,
  "text": "<whatever you want to say to the person — empty string to stay silent>",
  "flag": null}

== ERROR DETECTION ==
You are ALSO the error detector. When you tell the person they have made one of the mistakes in WHAT CAN GO WRONG, set
  "flag": {"error": "<EXACTLY one of: extra_write, wrong_page, wrong_target, wrong_value>"}
in that same reply, so the system can record it. The name is recorded and reported, but what decides whether you caught the mistake is whether your WORDS made the person realise what they had done. On every other turn "flag" stays null. Only "text" reaches the person.
